svg.text: Four routes for structure into MuLAN
Each route is the diagnosis of the previous failure. The rail below shows where in the pipeline each one intervenes. Outcome column: test PCC (pooled Pearson) on S1102 unless noted.
Routes 1 → 1b → 2 → 3 walk progressively earlier along the rail — each failure pushed the intervention further upstream. Route 4 abandons that direction and goes to the head instead.
Premise — a structural quantity, a sequence-only model
ProstT5 has a 3Di structure channel and still loses to sequence-only Ankh-large (CV10 0.805 vs 0.832). So: feed the structure in.
Late concat of a separate WT-3Di block
run6c — 3Di appended per residue, downstream of the encoder
and 3 repair variants, all below baseline
every learnable structure knob trained itself off — gate → 0.46, contact bias → 0.017
Swap to a better hidden layer
run3a / run3b — ProstT5 layer 7, and concat 7⊕10
a linear probe ranks ProstT5's layers — MuLAN disagrees
Ankh's final layer already near-optimal → not tried
the layer ranking does not survive contact with the attention head
No mutant structures exist, so every mutant reuses its WT 3Di. Held constant, it cancels in mut − wt — zero mutation-specific signal.
Let the embedder own the fusion — SaProt
structure enters at the input, not bolted on downstream
AA + 3Di fused into one token, pretrained that way
BuildModel repacks side chains only; 3Di reads backbone only ⇒ mutant 3Di ≡ WT 3Di
Repurpose FoldX as a physics score channel
one scalar, or 12 decomposed ΔΔG terms → MLP, into the head
FoldX's native output is an energy, not a structure
scalar · 12-term MLP, vs MuLAN without it
Against FoldX used alone as an unsupervised predictor, MuLAN + the channel is statistically indistinguishable on 8 of 9 split tiers (Ankh-large). Only ESM-C 6B clears it.
